verdict.rationale: Hoppscotch ships an official CLI for running API tests from a terminal or an automated system. Its `hopp test` command can produce JUnit reports for collection runs, which covers the core of running collections in CI. Nothing in the evidence documents the build-failure mechanism (non-zero exit codes on failed tests), so that half of the story is only implied by JUnit output. Missing for 10: documented exit-code/fail-the-build behavior, CI pipeline setup examples, independent hands-on corroboration of CI use.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run my API test collections in CI with a CLI and fail the build on regressions

citations.quote: The hopp test command now has the ability to generate a JUnit Report for collection runs in the CLI.

With the command-line interface (CLI) you can interact with the Hoppscotch platform using a terminal, or through an automated system. This enables you to run API tests, manage automated API monitoring
Use the Hoppscotch CLI to run API tests, automate monitoring, and manage collections from your terminal.
